subject: Cognitive Science
title: Regret and Anticipated Regret
description: A short lesson to help you apply Regret and Anticipated Regret.

hook.text: You miss a flight by 5 minutes and feel devastated. Miss it by 2 hours and you shrug. Same outcome, different pain.

buildup.text: Regret scales with how close you came to a better outcome. Near-misses sting more than distant ones.

discovery.text: We also feel more regret for actions than inactions—even when doing nothing costs more.

twist.text: Anticipated regret shapes future decisions. People avoid choices that might later make them feel bad.

climax.text: This drives loss aversion: the pain of losing feels twice as strong as the pleasure of winning the same amount.

punchline.text: We decide not just for outcomes—but to avoid future regret.

quiz.question: Why does missing a flight by 5 minutes hurt more than by 2 hours?
